blogs.title: Orthogonal Finetuning: A Gentle Introduction to Keeping Generative Models on Track
blogs.description: A plain‑English tour of Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT) for text‑to‑image models. Explains the core idea of finetuning by rotating weights rather than rewriting them, why that preserves a model’s visual “common sense,” and what this means for creators and developers.

blogs.title: Why Angles Matter: Hyperspherical Energy and the Secret Life of Neurons
blogs.description: Demystifies hyperspherical energy and pairwise neuron angles using simple analogies (like phase vs magnitude in images). Shows how keeping neuron directions intact preserves semantics, and why OFT’s angle‑preserving approach leads to better image quality.

blogs.title: COFT: Putting Guardrails on Finetuning for Stable, Predictable Results
blogs.description: Introduces Constrained Orthogonal Finetuning (COFT), which adds a small “radius” constraint around the original model. Covers how this improves stability, makes hyperparameters easier to set, and helps avoid model collapse while still adapting to new tasks.

blogs.title: Faster, Cheaper, and No Slower at Inference: The Efficiency Story of OFT
blogs.description: Breaks down why OFT trains quickly with few parameters (block‑diagonal orthogonal matrices), has smooth optimization, and adds zero inference overhead. Includes a high‑level look at Cayley transforms and why multiplying R into the weights keeps runtime unchanged.

blogs.title: OFT vs. LoRA vs. ControlNet: When to Use What for Text‑to‑Image Control
blogs.description: A practical comparison of popular finetuning strategies. Explains how OFT differs from LoRA’s low‑rank updates and ControlNet/T2I‑Adapter’s extra modules, with guidance on which approach fits subject personalization, edge/segmentation control, and pose tasks.

blogs.title: Personalizing Stable Diffusion with Only a Few Photos
blogs.description: Focuses on subject‑driven generation. Shows how OFT improves DreamBooth‑style personalization, preserving identity from a handful of images while following prompts more faithfully, converging faster, and remaining stable across training steps.

blogs.title: From Edges, Segments, and Landmarks to Photorealism
blogs.description: Covers controllable generation with OFT across Canny edges, segmentation maps, and facial landmarks. Explains the new control consistency metric (how well outputs match the control signal) and why OFT achieves stronger, more accurate control with fewer updates.

blogs.title: Under the Hood: Rotations at Scale with the Cayley Transform
blogs.description: A light technical deep dive into how OFT parameterizes rotations via the Cayley transform, why block‑diagonal structure keeps it memory‑friendly, and the trade‑offs and tips for implementation in large diffusion backbones.

blogs.title: Composing Skills by Multiplying Rotations: The Next Frontier of OFT
blogs.description: Explores forward‑looking ideas: composing multiple finetuned rotations for multi‑skill models, re‑scaled OFT for extra flexibility, and open challenges in scaling and parameter efficiency. Envisions toolchains where creative controls combine like Lego bricks.
